To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
starch metabolism, and in particular starch breakdown via the malate pathway, plays a role in stomatal opening in response to blue light.
starch metabolism, in addition to the photosynthesis-related functions, is required for full light-induced stomatal responses.
starch metabolism, and particularly the synthesis of a malate counter-ion to potassium, is required for full light-induced stomatal response to low blue light.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of starch in guard cell metabolism.
the effect of starch metabolism on stomatal opening and the role of blue and red light in this process.
the role of starch metabolism in stomatal responses to light.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
starch is required for the full expression of the blue-light-induced stomatal opening, and this effect is not mediated by changes in guard cell turgor.
starch metabolism in guard cells, via the synthesis and/or the degradation of malate, is involved in the stomata response to blue light.
the starch-deficient mutant plants are not only unable to store starch in their guard cells, but also that they lack the ability to synthesize malate in response to light.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the starch-deficient guard cells of Arabidopsis plants have a slower stomatal response to light than wild-type guard cells.

the guard cell chloroplasts are not only the sites of photosynthesis but also the sites of starch synthesis and degradation and that the starch metabolism is involved in the regulation of stomatal movements.

(a) starch metabolism is involved in stomatal responses to light; (b) starch metabolism is required for full response of stomata to blue light; (c) starch metabolism is not required for the full response of stomates to red light; and (d) starch metabolism is probably required for the full stomatal response under high chloride concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
starch metabolism is involved in stomatal opening, but only in the presence of blue light.
starch metabolism is required for the full stomatal response of Arabidopsis to blue light.
starch metabolism is involved in stomatal opening and closure in Arabidopsis thalina L.
